title: 6,000 cops, 2 notices, Dipke among 150 detained: How unrest unfolded in central Delhi
content: A protest march called 'Lehra Do Tiranga' saw widespread detentions by Delhi Police in Connaught Place. The event protested against the detention of Cockroach Janta Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Authorities restricted gatherings at Central Park due to a lack of official permission for the march. Parallel protests occurred near Mandi House, where demands for the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar arose.

title: US temple plot, school shooting: Gun epidemic spares no one as debate goes off target
content: A neo-Nazi teen attempted a mass shooting at a Hindu temple in Illinois, but his rifle jammed. The attack highlights ongoing debates about gun violence and societal issues, including parenting and mental health. Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi expressed horror that the attack targeted Indian Americans during worship. Many lawmakers condemned the incident, emphasizing the need to address religious and racial hatred in society.

title: No Jadeja, Iyer to lead in last two ODIs: Check full Test and ODI squads vs NZ
content: The BCCI selection committee has announced India's ODI and Test squads for the upcoming tour of New Zealand. India will play five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests on the tour. Fast bowlers Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj have returned to the Test squad. Shubman Gill will lead India in the first three ODIs, while Shreyas Iyer will captain the team in the last two matches.

title: 56-year-old chestnut grove, one of America’s last, at risk from AI data center
content: In West Virginia, plans for a new data center, the Monarch Compute Campus, could mean the removal of around 200 blight-resistant American chestnut trees. Planted in the 1970s, these trees are vital for future restoration projects. Conservationists express concern over the potential loss of this endangered genetic resource, making its fate precarious amidst development considerations and the push for sustainability.

title: ‘Don’t have to do this’: Trump tells new press secy Zacharia she can quit if she wants
content: Katie Zacharia has faced significant scrutiny after her brief tenure as White House press secretary. Donald Trump expressed concerns about the job's challenges and suggested she reconsider her position. The media has provided harsh coverage of her professional background and recent press briefing. Despite his doubts, Trump emphasized that the decision about her future is ultimately up to her.

title: Pennsylvania woman’s $250,000 family farm sale remains blocked after sibling dispute
content: Siblings are embroiled in a legal conflict over the fate of their family-owned 60-acre farm in Pennsylvania. A sister residing on the land sought to sell it despite having a long-term tenancy. In response, her siblings filed an urgent petition to block the sale, citing property rights. The Pennsylvania Superior Court supported the injunction, illustrating the complicated nature of co-ownership and informal familial arrangements in property disputes.

title: Return of Gulf oil: Has Iran lost grip on Hormuz & what does it mean for India?
content: The US war with Iran exposed Tehran’s ability to disrupt the global economy by blocking the Strait of Hormuz. Before the war, around 19 million barrels of crude oil were exported daily from the Middle East. However, September data from tanker-tracking firm Kpler showed oil flows recovering to an average of 16 million barrels per day, the highest since the conflict began.

title: 'Got 9 people murdered': On cam, big claim by Nitish's MLA; then clarification
content: Recalling his sacrifices for Nitish Kumar, Anant Snigh claimed: “Who has made as many sacrifices as I have? Nitish Kumar was nothing back then. He used to roam around here and there. At that time, while being with Nitish Kumar, I got nine people murdered,” Singh said. However, later the leader clarified that his remarks was misinterpreted and that he was referring to the killing of nine of his associates.

title: Deepti, debutant Niki rescue India after top-order collapse against Zimbabwe
content: India had to work harder than expected while chasing a target of 115, but recovered from losing four wickets for just 19 runs to reach the target with 4.2 overs to spare.

title: Curtains for Ravindra Jadeja in ODIs? All-rounder drops out of 2027 World Cup plans
content: Since the 2023 ODI World Cup, Ravindra Jadeja has featured in only 15 of the 32 ODIs India have played. In his last eight matches, he has picked up just three wickets at an economy rate of over six. Captain Shubman Gill has maintained that Jadeja was not dropped for the third ODI, but the 37-year-old is now fourth in the pecking order among India’s bowling all-rounders, behind Axar Patel, Washington Sundar and Harsh Dubey.

title: Drake approached over George Foreman’s $6m Texas mansion with 50-car garage
content: Drake could be adding another spectacular property to his Texas real estate portfolio, with the former mansion of boxing legend George Foreman hitting the market for $6 million. The sprawling estate features a nearly 12,000-square-foot mansion, an 11,000-square-foot collector’s garage capable of accommodating more than 50 cars, and the kitchen where Foreman filmed commercials for his famous grill. Although there is no confirmation that Drake plans to buy the property, the listing agent has reportedly contacted representatives for the rapper to gauge his interest.

title: Court tells US to process Green Card applications for up to 55k people
content: A federal judge has ordered the reopening of the diversity visa lottery for 2027, allowing 55,000 applicants. The ruling came after a lawsuit filed against Secretary of State Marco Rubio regarding the lottery's registration. Judge Jinsook Ohta mandated a 30-day registration period for submissions, which must meet eligibility requirements. Additionally, new policy changes require some applicants to return to their home countries for Green Card processing.

title: Why BCCI named two captains for India's New Zealand ODI series
content: India will have two captains during the five-match ODI series against New Zealand. Shubman Gill will lead the team in the first three matches, while Shreyas Iyer will take over for the final two games.

title: Kelce brothers’ Stoney Clover Lane deal: What’s changing for New Heights merch?
content: Jason and Travis Kelce have partnered with Stoney Clover Lane to launch a New Heights-inspired collection featuring clear stadium bags, a fanny pack, pouches and custom patches. The accessories celebrate the brothers' podcast and its 92 percenters fanbase while combining practical designs with playful details. Available through the Kelce Clubhouse, the collection coincides with the launch of its "Outta The House" hub and upcoming in-person fan events.

title: Jordan Spieth’s foundation donates $10M: How has it helped 137 community partners?
content: Jordan Spieth launched his family foundation early in his PGA Tour career, and a decade later it had surpassed $10 million in grants to 137 community partners. The foundation supports junior golf, pediatric cancer, individuals with special needs, and military families and veterans, with recent work including a $500,000 St. Jude grant and a Children’s Health endowment

title: Oh(io) No: Vivek Ramaswamy's Catch-22 problem with MAGA
content: Ramaswamy is running to become Ohio governor, a position he perhaps sees as a stepping stone to something bigger in the party. Yet Ramaswamy’s association with Trump is increasingly becoming a liability among neutral voters, while his faith and skin colour are proving a deterrent among parts of the MAGA base.

title: Zubeen Garg death case: Gauhati HC grants bail to suspended DSP Sandipon Garg
content: The Gauhati High Court has granted bail to Sandipon Garg, the suspended Assam Police DSP, linked to the controversial death of his cousin, Zubeen Garg. Arrested by the Special Investigation Team, Sandipon follows Amritprava Mahanta, the first accused, who also received bail. Additionally, the Supreme Court emphasized the need for an expedited trial for festival organizer Shyamkanu Mahanta amidst discussions on the nature of Zubeen's death—accidental or conspiratorial.

title: Zelenskyy slams Trump's diesel deal, says will help fund Putin’s war in Ukraine
content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has expressed concerns over the US diesel deal with Russia. He warned that this agreement could provide additional funds for Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine. Zelenskyy emphasized the need for Europe to increase support to Ukraine as missile attacks continue. The president requested significant financial assistance to maintain Ukraine's defense against Russian aggression.

title: SIR protests: Opposition has found common ground. But can it stay united?
content: Opposition parties in India are gradually uniting to support protests against the Chief Election Commissioner. Following arrests of CJP leaders, Rahul Gandhi showed solidarity, signaling a possible shift in strategy. Previously, Congress and CJP had organized separate protests over electoral issues, but they now seem to be collaborating more closely.

title: Putin, Trump to announce several joint projects as Russian diesel returns to market
content: Russia and the United States are set to announce new initiatives beyond their recent diesel agreement. Discussions reportedly include collaborative data centre projects powered by Russian nuclear energy. Supplies of diesel have begun reaching international markets following the deal with the United States. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has criticized the arrangement, expressing concerns about its implications for energy revenue.

title: Russian officer helped Ukraine kill over 300 troops by leaking military secrets
content: Russian army lieutenant Lev Stupnikov took a perilous stand against his own military by secretly supplying Ukrainian forces with critical intelligence. His actions led to the targeted elimination of more than 300 Russian soldiers and deliberate sabotage of weapons systems, culminating in his flight to the Russian Volunteer Corps as a direct challenge to Putin's leadership. Stupnikov’s bravery reshaped the landscape of the ongoing Ukraine conflict.

title: Shubman Gill returns to Ranji Trophy, set to play Punjab's next match
content: Shubman Gill is set to return to action for Punjab in the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season. He will play in the second-round match against Chhattisgarh starting on October 18. Gill missed the opening match against Assam, which was led by Uday Saharan. Recently, Gill was honored as the ICC Men's Player of the Month for the fifth time.

title: Oprah Winfrey’s $12m gift still supports Smithsonian theatre 13 years later
content: With a remarkable contribution of $13 million, Oprah Winfrey has solidified her legacy at the National Museum of African American History and Culture. Her financial support was instrumental in the museum's fundraising efforts, culminating in the naming of the Oprah Winfrey Theater. This theater serves as a vital space for public events, fostering discussions surrounding African American history and cultural narratives.

title: Michigan woman’s survivorship deed upheld over daughter’s challenge
content: A Michigan appeals court has confirmed the validity of a survivorship deed that granted ownership of a house to Jessica Rae Harless. The ruling asserts that Shirley Ann Page's 2012 deed established a joint tenancy with rights of survivorship. Despite Anita Lanctot's challenge regarding the absence of the term 'joint' in the deed, the court affirmed that Page's intent was unmistakably conveyed, ensuring Harless retains sole ownership of the property.

title: India flags trade concerns, market access barriers; China reacts
content: China has acknowledged India's concerns regarding trade barriers and the growing trade deficit during recent discussions. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman highlighted India's challenges in accessing the Chinese market for its products. The trade deficit with China widened significantly, reaching $105.93 billion in the first nine months of the year. India is striving to improve bilateral trade ties with China through negotiations and ongoing discussions.

title: 'We'll knock it out fast': Trump may target Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility
content: Donald Trump indicated that the US may target Iran's Pickaxe Mountain facility to deter nuclear weapon development. He stated that nuclear weapons would not be necessary for achieving US objectives in the situation. The remarks followed ongoing US-Israeli strikes against Iran since February, amid rising tensions. Iran's foreign ministry denied any nuclear activity at the site, labeling US threats as baseless.

title: 'Once again, an abduction': Aides claim Neha Bora taken to unknown location by cops
content: AISA chief Neha Bora was detained by Delhi Police while heading to a protest, and was taken to an unknown location. CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke was also detained at his residence shortly before the protest. Police stated the situation remained peaceful despite the detentions and heightened security in the capital. Hundreds of protesters gathered at Connaught Place and Mandi House, waving national flags.

title: Dravid slams 151 as Karnataka chase down 358; Sehwag scores 173 in losing cause
content: Anvay is captaining a 16-member Karnataka squad in the tournament, which began in Visakhapatnam earlier this month. His appointment as captain comes 10 months after he made his India U19 debut against Afghanistan in Sri Lanka in November last year.

title: In Claude we trust: Can 'God' save frontier models?
content: In this edition, we are going to look at how Anthropic is now hoping to get a little spiritual cred for its frontier models, and by doing so, they are channelling the kings of yore, who, despite their armies and gold, always wanted a divine mandate to rule. And will then ponder: how will we ever know when a machine becomes conscious?

title: MEA confirms Jaishankar-Rubio talks in Mumbai after Rahul’s jibe over India visit
content: MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal announced the engagements while responding to a question from news agency ANI about whether Jaishankar was expected to hold any meetings in Mumbai next week. He also explained that hosting foreign dignitaries outside the national capital was not unusual, pointing to previous engagements held in different Indian cities.

title: 'Snakebite' murder: UP court cites Manusmriti while pronouncing death sentence
content: In a chilling case, a local Meerut court handed down the death penalty to a woman and her accomplice for the heinous murder of her husband. To cover their tracks, they deceitfully placed a snake next to the deceased to simulate a snakebite. The court's decision drew on the Manusmriti and categorized the crime as 'rarest of rare.' The victim's family, having sought justice tirelessly, welcomed the verdict.

title: India diversified crude oil sources from 27 to 41 amid global disruptions: Puri
content: India has expanded its crude oil supply sources from 27 to 41 countries to improve energy security. The government is also increasing its refining capacity and exploring new oil sources in response to geopolitical concerns. Minister Hardeep Singh Puri emphasized the impact of global shipping disruptions on domestic industries and households. He outlined plans to enhance domestic energy production through initiatives like the Samudra Manthan scheme.

title: Connor McDavid's family: How his parents, brother and wife shaped his NHL career
content: Connor McDavid, the rising NHL superstar, has been helped shape by a family that has supported his development, discipline and life away from hockey. His parents, Brian and Kelly McDavid, encouraged his early dreams, while older brother Cameron provided a competitive edge. He continues his career as captain of the Edmonton Oilers, and his wife, Lauren Kyle, has become a big part of his life personally.

title: Caitlin Clark's family: How her parents and siblings shaped her WNBA journey
content: Caitlin Clark’s road to WNBA stardom was paved by a family that supported her basketball dreams early on; and her father, Brent Clark, taught her the basics and her mother, Anne Clark, gave her emotional support, and her brothers, Blake and Colin, added a competitive element to her upbringing, helping to shape the determination and athletic drive behind her rise.

title: A slice of Andhra in US: Texas emerges as a hub for grand Telugu weddings
content: Telugu families in the US no longer need to travel to India for a traditional wedding. Texas, especially Austin, Frisco and Dallas, is emerging as a top destination, thanks to a booming ecosystem of purohits, caterers, planners, photographers and sprawling NRI-owned venues. From turmeric roots to betel leaves, every ritual essential is available locally, helping the diaspora preserve age-old customs, avoid visa hassles and celebrate with friends and relatives nearby.

title: How much gold and silver can you legally keep at home?
content: In a recent case before the ITAT Mumbai, the Income Tax Department carried out searches at a woman's residence and bank lockers, and seized diamonds, gold and silver articles, along with jewellery, which it treated as unexplained assets. The seized items included gold jewellery of 427.71 grams, 258 grams of pure gold, diamond-studded jewellery containing 161.33 grams of gold, and articles made of a silver mixture weighing 11.200 kg.

title: Texas woman turned homemade soda into Poppi; PepsiCo later bought it for $1.95bn
content: Allison Ellsworth began making homemade soda in her Texas kitchen to address her digestive concerns before selling it at farmers’ markets. After appearing on Shark Tank and building Poppi through social media, her business grew to over $500 million in annual revenue. In 2025, PepsiCo acquired the prebiotic soda brand for $1.95 billion.

title: 'I am alone, broke no law': Dipke argues with Delhi cops as they detain him - watch
content: Dipke, earlier today, had defended the party's protests, asserting that peaceful demonstrations were a democratic right. He accused the government of restricting citizens' freedoms and disrupting business activities through shutdowns, Internet suspensions and movement restrictions. "I'm alone, what law did I break," Dipke asked before he was detained. The court had directed the CJP to refrain from causing any public disturbance for a period of one year.

title: Dehradun to host the Times of India Sports Awards on December 6
content: The Times of India Sports Awards (TOISA) will return for its ninth edition in Dehradun on December 6, 2026. The awards will recognise India’s sporting achievements across disciplines, with the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya and the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow among the major events shaping the year. The ceremony will bring together athletes and teams whose performances have represented India on national and international stages.

title: Jeremy Renner bought LA mansion for $7m, transformed it and sold for $24m
content: Jeremy Renner and Kristoffer Winters transformed a 1920s mansion into an expansive, design-led estate . the property, known as The Reserve, was originally acquired by the pair in 2010 for $7 million . three years later, their transformation of the estate had resulted in a 10,005-square-foot residence that eventually attracted British luxury property developer Nick Candy .
